chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from a number of our companions from Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah, who said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who performs Tawaf and joins two circuits (usbu') together. He said, 'If you wish, I will narrate to you from the people of al-Madinah.' I said, 'By Allah, I do not have a need for that; I am your ransom, but narrate to me what I am obliged to do by Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.' He said, 'Do not join two circuits; whenever you complete one circuit, pray two rak'ahs. As for me, perhaps I join the third and fourth.' I looked at him, and he said, 'I am with these (people).'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ: the people of al-Madinah (referring to a specific group or location's practice)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to perform Tawaf circuits and the associated prayers according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between the obligatory act of praying two rak'ahs after each circuit and the optional act of joining circuits (qarn) without prayer, which he permits as a flexible practice. His remark, 'I am with these,' highlights the scholarly principle of adhering to the consensus of the people of Medina while maintaining personal discretion, reflecting the Shia methodology of balancing strict adherence with practical ease in ritual worship.
